# The Lights That Keep Their Watch

## Scripture

*"When I consider your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars, which you have set in place, what is mankind that you are mindful of them, human beings that you care for them?"* — Psalm 8:3–4 (NIV)

## Reflection

Step outside on a clear November evening and you'll notice something steady: the same bright stars return to the same places, night after night, season after season. Orion climbs the eastern sky. The Big Dipper dips low in the north. Astronomers call this the "clockwork of the heavens"—the quiet, dependable turning of the cosmos.

There's deep comfort in that faithfulness. The stars don't check in on our moods or adjust themselves to our circumstances. They simply keep their watch, just as they have since before Abraham, just as they will long after we are gone.

David looked at that same sky and felt small—but not forgotten. "What is mankind," he wondered, "that you are mindful of them?" The God who keeps the stars in their courses also bends low to notice us. He numbers the hairs of our heads. He hears the prayers we can barely form. The same hand that set the moon in place holds our lives with even greater care.

This autumn, let the returning constellations remind you: God's faithfulness does not waver with the seasons of your heart. He kept His watch over the heavens long before you were born, and He will keep His watch over you.

## Prayer

Lord of the spinning heavens, thank You that the stars keep their watch—and that You keep watch over me. When my own faith feels small and shifting, remind me that Your faithfulness is as steady as the lights above. Amen.
